title: You thought it was God.
paragraphs:
You thought it was God.
But you never prayed.
And now you’re living inside a decision you can’t undo.

It looked right.
It sounded peaceful.
It felt safe.

But something in your spirit…
was silent.
Because urgency felt louder than obedience.
Because deep down… you believed you could handle it without God.

Joshua 9 doesn’t show a wicked leader.
It shows a confident one.
The Gibeonites didn’t come with swords.

Worn-out sandals.
Cracked wineskins.
Dry bread that looked ancient.
“The men took some of their provisions, but did not ask counsel from the LORD.” — Joshua 9:14

They looked.
They tasted.
They evaluated.
And that is still how many of us fall today.
But because we move without Him.
You didn’t pray before the relationship.
Now you’re emotionally entangled with someone God never confirmed.
You didn’t pray before the decision.
Now you’re carrying consequences you didn’t foresee.
You didn’t pray before saying yes.
Now your peace is gone… and you don’t know why.
This is the danger of surface-level discernment.
But it’s actually self-reliance in disguise.
“Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make straight your paths.”
Because partial surrender still leads to misdirection.

You can be sincere…
and still be wrong.

You can be spiritual…
and still be deceived.

You can even be chosen by God…
and still make unprayed decisions that shape your future.
Joshua was not rejected by God.
But he still had to live with the covenant he made.
Maybe this is hitting deeper than you expected.
That quiet check in your spirit.
Because we often trust visible evidence more than invisible guidance.
We trust what we can touch more than what God speaks.
But here’s where grace breaks in.
Because the story doesn’t end in failure.
He didn’t walk away from Joshua.
The Gibeonites became servants in the house of God.
was still woven into God’s greater purpose.
God is not limited by your mistakes.
And this is where Jesus steps in.
Because Joshua points to a deeper need.
Where Joshua made a covenant without prayer…
Jesus made a covenant with His blood.
“Therefore He is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance.”
Our greatest deception is not just bad decisions.
It’s the lie that we can live without God.
And no amount of human wisdom can fix that.
He lived the life we couldn’t live.
He died the death we deserved.
And He rose again—so your story doesn’t end in failure.
But God made a way back to Himself—through Christ.
It is dependence on the Spirit of God.
And if you’ve already made the mistake?
If you’re already living in the consequence?
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
There is still a way forward.
God can redeem what you rushed.
God can heal what you mishandled.
God can restore what deception distorted.
What decision are you making without prayer?
What “good opportunity” have you never surrendered to God?
Let this be your moment of surrender.
It might save them from a silent regret.
And if this stirred something in you…
